title: I2C (SparkFun Learn)
why: Why I2C uses two wires with open-drain drivers, start and stop conditions, ACK and NACK, addressing and clock stretching.
caveat: Written for hobbyists. It links to the NXP I2C specification (UM10204) for interview-level depth.

title: Pull-up Resistors (SparkFun Learn)
why: What pull-up resistors do, why floating inputs need them, and how to pick a value with Ohm's law. This is the part of I2C people get asked about.

title: Serial Peripheral Interface (SPI) (SparkFun Learn)
why: SPI as a synchronous bus: clock, data and chip select lines, controller and peripheral roles, wiring several devices.
caveat: Does not cover clock polarity and phase modes by name. Read a device datasheet next.

title: Serial Communication (SparkFun Learn)
why: Asynchronous serial and UARTs: start, data, parity and stop bits, baud rate, TTL versus RS-232, with a worked 9600 8N1 example.

title: How to Use an Oscilloscope (SparkFun Learn)
why: The display, vertical and horizontal controls, triggers and probes, and a first measurement.

title: How to Use a Multimeter (SparkFun Learn)
why: Measuring voltage, resistance, current and continuity step by step, with safety notes.
caveat: SparkFun marks this page as retired, so product links may be out of date.

title: How to Read a Schematic (SparkFun Learn)
why: Standard symbols for resistors, capacitors, diodes, transistors and ICs, and how nets and net names show connections.

title: How to Read Datasheets and Application Notes (Circuit Basics)
why: How datasheets are organized and what each section is for, walked through with a sample datasheet, then how application notes show a part in use.
caveat: Assumes some familiarity with terms like pinout. The page has ads and affiliate links.

title: How To Read A Datasheet (Electronics with Becky Stern, DigiKey)
why: What the charts, tables and specs in a component datasheet mean, so you can pick parts with more confidence.
caveat: The page does not state the video length.

title: Voltage, Current, Resistance, and Ohm's Law (SparkFun Learn)
why: Voltage, current and resistance with a water analogy, Ohm's law, and an LED with a current-limiting resistor worked through.

title: Logic Levels (SparkFun Learn)
why: Logic levels, TTL versus 3.3 V CMOS thresholds (VIH, VOL), active-high and active-low pins, and level shifting.

title: Digital Logic Gate Tutorial (Electronics Tutorials)
why: Basic logic gates, TTL and CMOS families, and logic levels.
caveat: Only a brief mention of Boolean algebra. The IC-family sections are dense for absolute beginners.

title: Capacitors (SparkFun Learn)
why: How capacitors work, with a section on decoupling (bypass) capacitors that filter supply noise next to ICs.
caveat: The theory section gets harder toward the end. Beginners can skip the calculus.

title: PCB Basics (SparkFun Learn)
why: What a PCB is, its layers (base, copper, solder mask, silkscreen), common terms, and short tips for designing one.

title: KiCad documentation
why: The official KiCad documentation. It links a Getting Started guide and the user manual for the current version.

title: Buck converter (Wikipedia)
why: How a step-down DC-DC converter works, with continuous and discontinuous mode, efficiency losses, and synchronous and multiphase variants.
caveat: An encyclopedia article, not a tutorial.

title: Basic Calculation of a Buck Converter's Power Stage (Texas Instruments, SLVA477)
why: The formulas for sizing the inductor and capacitors of a buck converter power stage in continuous conduction mode.
caveat: A 9 page PDF. It says it does not explain how a buck converter works, so read the Wikipedia article first.

title: Fundamentals of MOSFET and IGBT Gate Driver Circuits (Texas Instruments, SLUA618A)
why: A systematic approach to designing high-performance gate drive circuits for MOSFETs and IGBTs.
caveat: A 48 page PDF, so use the contents list to read only what you need.

title: Electromagnetic compatibility (Wikipedia)
why: Emissions versus immunity, and the general ideas of grounding, shielding and filtering.
caveat: An encyclopedia article. Layout guidance is only general, see the Texas Instruments note for a PCB example.

title: Several common PCB design techniques (Texas Instruments Analog Design Journal, SLYT849)
why: Reducing EMI in PCB design: grounding, bypass capacitors, trace routing and layer stacking, with a worked layout example.

title: Pro Git (Scott Chacon and Ben Straub)
why: A free book on Git from basic version control and daily commands through branching and workflows. It applies to hardware projects the same way.
caveat: Licensed CC BY-NC-SA 3.0. The second edition dates from 2014.

title: Beej's Guide to C Programming
why: A free C tutorial in HTML and PDF.
caveat: The page calls itself a beta-quality document with possible errors. I did not confirm which topics it covers.

title: Learn C (learn-c.org)
why: Free interactive C lessons from the basics (variables, arrays, loops, functions) to pointers, structures, dynamic allocation and unions, with a Bitmasks chapter.
caveat: The site says it is still under construction and promotes a paid course.

title: Learn C++ (learncpp.com)
why: A free structured course in modern C++ from first program to templates, exceptions and smart pointers. No programming experience needed.
